name: NoveltyBench
ability_definition: The ability to come up with unusual or clever ideas about a given topic or situation, or to develop creative ways to solve a problem.

task_realism.reasoning: A minority of prompts, such as creative writing and subjective or brainstorming-style queries, resemble real idea-generation work. Many others ask for die rolls, random picks or underspecified trivia like naming an African capital. Those tasks do not resemble workplace problems that call for clever or unusual solutions.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Prompts are short and context-free, with no domain constraints, stakeholders, tools or iteration. Scoring samples 10 independent generations and checks whether they are distinct from one another. Real work usually asks for one or a few strong, contextually fitting novel ideas, and those ideas are judged against what is typical in the field.

construct_coverage.reasoning: The benchmark mainly measures output diversity across samples, which is closer to fluency or flexibility than to originality. A reward model adds a quality weighting, but nothing directly judges cleverness, unusualness compared with human norms, or creative problem-solving. Feasibility and domain breadth for real problems are also largely absent.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs and outputs are free-form natural language rather than multiple choice or toy grids, which partly resembles real ideation artifacts. The meaningful unit of evaluation, however, is a set of 10 samples partitioned by an equivalence classifier. That structure is artificial and not how creative work products are delivered or assessed.

transferability_reasoning: NoveltyBench rewards models for producing distinct, reasonable-quality answers across repeated samples of simple prompts, many of which involve randomness or trivia rather than problem solving. It uses open-ended text but does not assess the cleverness, relative unusualness or workable creativity that define Originality at work. It is best treated as a weak proxy.

2026.model_or_system: Novamine AI (inference-time system built on claude-opus-5)
2026.metric: utility@10 (NoveltyBench cumulative utility, 0-10 scale), pooled over all 1,100 prompts (NB-Curated + NB-WildChat)
2026.human_reference: General educated adult workforce doing open-ended brainstorming or ideation (e.g., asked to produce 10 different good answers, ideas or short creative pieces for a prompt)
